_instructions.task: Translate every 'en' value into: uk (Ukrainian), de (German), es (Spanish), fr (French), pt (Brazilian Portuguese), nb (Norwegian Bokmål), fi (Finnish), nl (Dutch). Add each translation as a field next to 'en' (e.g. "uk": "..."). Return the SAME JSON structure, do not change any 'key' values — they are identifiers.
_instructions.voice: Warm, calm, adult-to-adult. Never nagging, never shaming, no corporate tone. Informal address everywhere it's natural (ти / du / tu / você). Write like a native copywriter, not a translator — rhythm and idiom over literalness.
brand_rules: App name 'Tempa' is never translated or declined.
Ukrainian: modern natural Ukrainian, no russian calques. If ADHD ever comes up it is РДУГ (it does not appear in these strings).
German: du-form. ADHD would be ADHS (does not appear here).
Keep placeholders exactly: %@ is substituted at runtime (a first name, or an hour value like '3'). Position it naturally for the language.
Keep '!!!', '(247)', '·', quotes and dashes in the spirit of the original — they are design, adapt the quote style to the language norm.
Gender-neutral phrasing everywhere: the reader may be any gender. Avoid past-tense first-person forms that force gender (e.g. Ukrainian 'зробив/зробила') — rephrase instead.

special_cases.weeks a year / weeks of the year: Both label the big number on the math screen ('≈7 weeks a year'). Languages that decline nouns after numerals use TWO forms: 'weeks of the year' is shown for counts 2–4, 'weeks a year' for 5+. In Ukrainian that is 'тижні на рік' vs 'тижнів на рік'. Languages without this distinction translate both identically.
special_cases.%@h: Compact hour unit shown as '3h' / '1.5h'. Use the shortest natural unit: uk '%@ год', de '%@ Std.', fr/es/pt '%@ h', nb '%@ t', fi '%@ h', nl '%@ u'.
special_cases.yesterday: A tiny red overdue badge on a task row — one lowercase word.
